label: source_measurements

source.title: Effect of Styrene-Diene Block Copolymers and Glass Bubbles on the Post-Consumer Recycled Polypropylene Properties

material.recycled_input: Post-consumer rPP collected from post-user injection-moulded boxes by a Romanian collector
material.filler: 3M Glass Bubbles S22, soda lime borosilicate glass

varied_input.name: Glass Bubbles S22 addition
varied_input.level_origin: no-added-GB reference inferred from dash and formulation label

process.forming: Compression-moulded sheets; mechanical specimens cut from those sheets

test_method.source_location: sec2dot5dot6-materials-13-00543, tensile-properties paragraph and final environment statement

observations.sample_count_kind: tensile specimens (source calls them samples) per blend
observations.product_question: At this tested glass-bubble level within this source matrix family, is the reported mean tensile strength at break inside a stated target? Individual-specimen or finished-product compliance cannot be checked.
limits: Only source-reported means and standard deviations are retained; the five individual specimen values and observed min/max are unavailable.
Standard deviation is not an observed range, a confidence interval, a tolerance or a future-batch prediction.
SBS and SIS are separate matrix families. Do not pool them or interpolate between tested glass-bubble levels.
Source composition columns mix wt% for the polymer components and vol.% for glass bubbles. These labels are preserved; no amount-basis conversion is inferred.
The two zero-added-filler references use a source dash in the GB column. Numeric zero is a reference-level interpretation, not an extracted numeric cell.
The source does not establish independent production batches or a result for the user's recycled input or finished product.
No density, mass, acoustic property, porosity effect or finished-product consistency is calculated from these tensile results.
